thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: hosted-api: elevated 5xx rate detected (gateway 502/504/timeouts). Severity: P1. Triggered at 2026-03-14T04:20:00Z. Current 5xx ~6.5% over 5m on /v1/chat and /v1/generate. Paging lina-g (on-call) and escalation to eng-sre if no ack in 3m. Links: /dash/hosted-api/errors, /runbooks/control-plane-failures

lina-g: ack — I'm on. quick visibility: any deploys in the last 30m? customer reports?

harry-p: I see a correlated spike of 504s pointing to control-plane endpoints: /auth/verify and /orgs/resolve. Traces show p95 auth latency jumped to ~3.8s. Gateway started returning 502s when auth timed out.

michael-s: pulling logs now. sample entries:
```
2026-03-14T04:19:56Z gateway id=g-77 upstream=auth-svc status=504 latency=3810ms id=xyz
2026-03-14T04:20:01Z gateway id=g-81 upstream=org-lookup status=502 err="upstream_timeout" latency=3950ms
```

jess-l: no deploys to gateway. deploy-bot, any control-plane releases between 03:50-04:20?

deploy-bot: [04:03 UTC] Deploy started: control-plane/org-lookup v2.4.0 -> v2.5.0 by michael-s
deploy-bot: [04:05 UTC] Deploy finished: control-plane/org-lookup v2.5.0

michael-s: I rolled a small change to org-lookup to switch storage client to pooled connections. Maybe pool sizing issue under burst. Hypothesis: connection saturation -> long waits -> timeouts.

lina-g: temp mitigation: can we disable new client via feature flag? If not, consider rollback. Also, enable gateway caching of org lookups for short TTL to reduce control-plane fanout.

jess-l: checking feature flag system... flag exists: org_lookup_v2.5_enabled=true. Turning it off now.
```
# set flag
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/flags/org_lookup_v2.5_enabled -d '{"value":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN"
```

jess-l: flag flipped. monitoring metrics...

support-bot: inbound: spike of 5xx noted in support queue. 9 customer mentions in last 8m, region eu-west-1 and us-east-1.

harry-p: after flag flip: control-plane request rate to org-lookup dropped ~68%. p95 auth latency falling from 3.8s -> 420ms over 90s. Gateway 5xx dropped from 6.5% -> 1.6%. Looks promising.

michael-s: good. But rolling back the client change requires longer testing. Plan: keep flag off, revert deploy in next maintenance window. For immediate hardening I'm enabling a short gateway-local cache TTL=20s and a circuit breaker that fails open when control-plane p50 > 400ms. Also will apply a DB connection cap in org-lookup's config to prevent pool blowout. Opening PRs now.

lina-g: please also throttle requests from heavy orgs to control-plane, and coordinate account teams for top-impacted customers. Support, compile list of org ids by 5xx counts.

support-bot: top orgs by 5xx in last 15m: org-321 (37%), org-876 (21%), org-219 (8%), org-602 (6%). Creating cases and pinging AE for org-321 and org-876.

jess-l: gateway config change applied:
```
gateway.conf:
  org_lookup_cache_ttl: 20s
  org_lookup_cache_capacity: 5000
  control_plane_circuit_breaker_ms: 400
  org_lookup_fail_open: true
```

jess-l: also toggled a temporary rate limiter on control-plane endpoints: 200 reqs/sec aggregated.

michael-s: DB metrics show connection spike matched the deploy start time. Rolling back the deploy would be safest but flag flip is stable. We'll schedule a rollback to v2.4.0 in canary during low traffic. For now mitigation = feature flag off + gateway cache + rate limits + conn cap config.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied (feature flag off, gateway cache, rate-limiter). Error rate decreasing. Continue monitoring.

lina-g: customer comms draft: "We observed elevated 5xx errors affecting API requests. Immediate mitigation applied. Root cause appears to be a control-plane service change that increased latency; we have disabled the change and are monitoring. We'll follow up with a postmortem and list of impacted orgs." Approve?

support-bot: draft posted to #support-customer-alerts. AE for org-321 notified.

harry-p: plan for post-incident: 1) postmortem with root cause, 2) add canary checks for pool saturation, 3) automated feature-flag rampdown if upstream latencies exceed threshold, 4) gateway-side fail-open for critical control-plane lookups. Assigning postmortem to michael-s.

michael-s: I accept postmortem owner. Will include retrospective on testing/monitoring gaps and a fix timeline.

lina-g: handoff: I'm out in 18m. harry, you take on-call after that. I'll document timeline and confirm support outreach completed.

harry-p: taking over. I've pinned dashboards and raised temporary alert suppression to avoid flapping. Escalate to eng-sre if errors >2% for >5m.

deploy-bot: NOTE: a pending canary rollback scheduled at 05:10 UTC to revert control-plane/org-lookup to v2.4.0 in canary zone. Manual approval required.

jess-l: rollback to canary started and finished; canary metrics look normal. Proceeding with staged rollback at 05:20 if canary remains green.

support-bot: confirmations: messages sent to org-321 and org-876 contacts. Support cases created.

lina-g: status update for incident tracker: mitigated — immediate symptoms reduced via feature flag and gateway changes. Impact window ~12 minutes for high-error orgs; broader elevated 5xx for ~30 minutes. No customer data access issue identified. Postmortem owner: michael-s. Follow-up meeting scheduled in 90 minutes.

harry-p: monitoring looks stable. I'll keep an eye on any regressions and make sure the canary rollback continues.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: primary symptoms abated. Keep monitoring for 1h and attach postmortem link when ready.

michael-s: I'll start the postmortem doc and include action items: fix pool sizing behavior in org-lookup client, add canary load tests, implement auto-rollback for risky feature flags, and add a sentinel metric on control-plane queue depth.

lina-g: signing out. harry, you're on. thanks team.

harry-p: acknowledged. will escalate if anything reappears.
